hooks.text: For centuries, the most toxic planet hid a secret halo.
Why does a toxic planet look like a glowing halo?
One rare celestial transit reveals a planet's secret fire ring.

title: The Secret Halo of Venus
description: Discover how a rare celestial alignment revealed the toxic atmosphere of Venus through a stunning ring of fire.

beats.text: For centuries, the most toxic planet hid a secret halo.
beats.visual: NASA Solar Dynamics Observatory high-resolution image of the 2012 transit of Venus

beats.text: It only appears when Venus passes directly across the Sun.
beats.visual: Diagram of the solar system showing Venus passing between Earth and the Sun

beats.text: Observers first spotted this hair-thin ring of light in 1761.
beats.visual: Historical illustration of the 1761 transit of Venus showing a luminous arc

beats.text: They watched a dark silhouette touch the solar edge.
beats.visual: Telescopic photograph of the silhouette of Venus against the Sun's disk

beats.text: Mikhail Lomonosov realized this fire ring was actually refracted sunlight.
beats.visual: Portrait of Mikhail Lomonosov, the scientist who discovered Venus's atmosphere

beats.text: The light was bending through a massive, thick atmosphere.
beats.visual: Scientific diagram of light refraction through a planetary atmosphere

beats.text: This was our first proof that another world had air.
beats.visual: NASA artist concept of the thick yellowish clouds of Venus

beats.text: This halo proved Venus is a hellscape of acid clouds and crushing pressure.
beats.visual: NASA artist concept of the dense and hazy surface of Venus

beats.text: The solar system's most toxic planet hides a secret halo.
beats.visual: Amateur telescopic photograph of Venus in its thin crescent phase showing a slight arc

better_than_last: This script prioritizes the 1761 atmospheric discovery over Galileo's biography to reach the payoff faster, applying the lesson from ep165.
